subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Disturbances: Fighting the Unexpected
description: A fast breakdown of Disturbances: Fighting the Unexpected for builders.

hook.text: You open a window on a cold day. The room temperature drops. The heater must compensate.

buildup.text: A disturbance is any external change that pushes the output away from the setpoint.

discovery.text: Feedback control handles disturbances automatically — the error signal grows, and the controller reacts.

twist.text: Feedforward control anticipates disturbances. If a sensor detects the open window, it boosts heating immediately.

climax.text: Industrial processes combine feedback and feedforward — react to the known, correct the unknown.

punchline.text: Disturbances push systems off target. Good control pushes back faster.

quiz.question: How does feedforward control differ from feedback control?
options: Feedforward measures the output; feedback measures the input
Feedforward anticipates disturbances before they affect the output; feedback reacts after
Feedforward is always more accurate than feedback control
